methodology.summary: Each row is a protocol family in one category (DefiLlama children with the same parent are summed, so Aave V2/V3/V4 are one row). The candidate pool is the union of DefiLlama's top 200 rows by TVL, CoinGecko's top 200 tokens by market cap and the top 20 rows in every category (267 rows); percentiles are computed inside that pool. The score is a weighted sum of percentiles across the pool: size 0.3226, 6-month relative TVL growth 0.2258, 6-month TVL added in dollars 0.1828, 30-day fees momentum 0.1075, 30-day DEX volume momentum 0.0753, token attention (24h turnover) 0.086, plus a small bonus per distinct X post from the user's lists. Percentiles cannot saturate, so a fresh listing cannot jump the board on a capped growth number. A family with no TVL 180 days ago is marked New: its relative growth is neutral and it is judged on the dollars it has gathered. CoinGecko turnover sits beside DefiLlama, as a percentile across the 70 rows with a mapped token (turnover and netflow are divided by market cap). An unmapped row scores a neutral 0.5. Nansen smart money is off in this build. CEX, Ponzi and token-locker rows are excluded.

Pre-checks: the vault's `provisioner()` and `feeCalculator()` are the documented ones, async USDC deposits are enabled and the vault is not paused. Asserts the user's USDC and the Provisioner's USDC move by exactly the amount and `asyncRequestHashes` holds `getRequestHash` of the request; after the deadline `refundRequest` returns exactly the USDC, clears the hash, and the user holds no units. Solving is done by Aera's solver off this machine
